task.description:
WF-03 Step 3 for ISS-0117: write the amendment. You are the PRODUCER; REVIEWER gates your output at Step 3b and has FAILED this class of change before, so write it to be re-derived, not skimmed.

READ FIRST: handoffs/WF03-ISS0117-20260821/step-01-diagnose.json's `result.summary`. It is the specification for this step and it is measured, not asserted — ORCH independently re-derived its load-bearing counts before dispatching you (534 handoff files, 15 illegal `status` values, 13 stray-key files, 2 stale handoffs, 3 distinct ad-hoc recovery keys, `last_known_step` used 64x in registry.json and defined nowhere in docs/, zero agent-death vocabulary across the four doc surfaces). Treat its section (D) as the agreed answers and its sections (A)-(C) as the evidence you cite. Where the diagnosis and ISS-0117 disagree, the diagnosis wins — it measured, the issue record did not; its divergences D-1..D-4 are listed in the Step 1 handoff's result.issues.

THE ROOT CAUSE YOU ARE FIXING, stated so you do not fix the smaller version of it: HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 3's ownership table binds ONLY the three timestamp fields. There is no row for `result` and none for `status`. So 'a handoff's result is the acting agent's own attested report' — the assumption the entire gate model rests on — is nowhere written as a rule, and therefore has no exception clause. That silence is why four runs improvised four incompatible repairs under three different key names. Do not write a section that merely covers agent death while leaving the table silent; the table is the defect.

WRITE THESE SIX CHANGES.

(1) HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 3 — extend the ownership table. Add a `status` row and a `result` row naming the acting agent as owner. Add an exception pointer on `completed_at`, `status` and `result` to the new section from (2). Evidence to cite: WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-final-git-merge.json's `completed_at` (2026-08-21T03:29:36Z) is byte-identical to its `orch_reconstruction.reconstructed_at` — ORCH wrote a field the table assigns to 'the receiving agent', and the marker did not declare it. Even the best-executed repair so far silently violated text already in force.

(2) HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md — a NEW section (place it as 4.1, immediately after section 4 'Complete the handoff', which it is the exception to) covering a handoff whose acting agent stopped existing. It must decide all four of ISS-0117's questions, in this shape:

  (a) WHO MAY COMPLETE IT — a split answer keyed to whether the step's own side effects finished, and explicitly NOT 'nobody'. If side effects are INCOMPLETE: ORCH re-stamps the handoff to PENDING with a fresh clock read and dispatches a FRESH INSTANCE OF THE SAME ROLE, which writes its own attested result normally. State that `rework_count` is NOT incremented — ORCHESTRATOR.md section 5's counter tracks REJECTED work, and nothing was rejected. This has a worked precedent to cite: WF02-REQ027-20260816/step-02d-reviewer.json's `orch_restart_note`, which ruled exactly this and has sat in one handoff file ever since instead of in the protocol. If side effects are COMPLETE AND IRREVERSIBLE (a merge landed, a branch is gone), redispatch is impossible — there is nothing left to do — so ORCH, and ONLY ORCH, writes the result block under (b)'s marking. Refute 'leave it IN_PROGRESS forever' by naming the measurement, not by preference: WF02-REQ043-20260818/step-final-git-merge.json is that option executed, and it has read PENDING with a null result since 2026-08-18 for a run that squash-merged to main as e25822a via PR #174 — an audit trail actively asserting something false, with the truth surviving only inside a registry.json prose note.

  (b) THE MANDATORY MARKING — a REQUIRED TOP-LEVEL FIELD with a fixed name and a fixed object shape, not a convention and not prose in a summary. Name it `not_agent_attested`. Required members: `reconstructed_by`, `reconstructed_at` (clock-read), `reason`, `fields_written` (the EXPLICIT list of fields this writer authored, e.g. ["status","completed_at","result"]), `evidence` (the commands run and what each established), `not_verifiable_after_the_fact` (an explicit list — never an empty implication). Specify it as OPTIONAL-BY-ABSENCE: present only on a recovered handoff, so all 534 existing files stay valid and no backfill is forced. Add it to section 2's JSON schema block. `fields_written` is the member that must not be dropped — D-3 in the diagnosis shows the best prior instance reconstructed `completed_at` without declaring it. Justify the required-field-over-convention choice with the measurement rather than the issue's assertion: the convention produced THREE key names across FIVE occurrences (`orch_timestamp_correction` x2, `orch_restart_note`, `orch_reconstruction`), applied at two different key positions, and changed shape from string to object between its first and second use. A convention that changed shape on its second application is not a convention. Note honestly that a written rule is necessary and NOT sufficient — section 2's `status` enum IS written down and 15 files violate it — but that a named field is at least greppable, which prose in a summary is not.

  (c) DIED-MID-ACTION vs DIED-AFTER-ACTING — state that these need materially different paths ((a)'s two branches) and that the discrimination is a MANDATORY PROBE OF THE STEP'S DECLARED SIDE EFFECTS, never a judgement call and never read off the handoff's own contents. This is the hard part and the evidence says so: WF02-REQ043-20260818 (power outage mid-rebase) and WF03-ISS0109-20260821 (API error after the merge landed) present IDENTICALLY on disk — both a handoff with a null result — and needed opposite treatments. Give the git-step probe set as the worked example, lifting it from WF03-ISS0109's own `orch_reconstruction.commands_run`: `ls .git/rebase-merge .git/rebase-apply` (a mid-rebase leaves these; their absence is the most direct mid-action discriminator), `git status --short` plus `git branch --show-current`, `git rev-list --left-right --count origin/main...HEAD`, `git ls-remote --heads origin <branch>`, `gh pr view <n> --json state,mergedAt,mergeCommit`. Then generalize: every step type declares an idempotent completion predicate over its own side effects, and classification is the OUTPUT of evaluating it. State two constraints explicitly: INDETERMINATE FALLS TO REDISPATCH (redispatching an already-complete idempotent step is cheap; attesting to an incomplete one puts a false PASS into the audit trail), and whatever the probes cannot settle goes into `not_verifiable_after_the_fact` rather than being omitted — silence about an unverifiable thing reads as verification.

  (d) A cross-reference to (3) below for the run-level record.

(3) ORCHESTRATOR.md — the run-level record. Add a discrete `recovered: true` field plus a `recovery_note` (naming the affected step file and which branch of (a) was applied) to registry.json's run entry shape, NOT prose folded into `last_known_step`. Cite why: `last_known_step` holds unbounded prose, and WF02-REQ043-20260818's interruption IS recorded there — buried in a ~1,000-character note — which is exactly why a scan found the stale handoff and not the interruption. Reconcile with, do not contradict, ISS-0033's established precedent that an interrupted run's ORIGINAL entry is left untouched and a resume is recorded as a SEPARATE APPENDED entry with a `-resume` run_id suffix: state which mechanism applies when. The diagnosis recommends a same-session recovery amends the entry and a later-session recovery appends a `-resume` entry; adopt that unless you can show it wrong, and say so either way. Both HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 5 and core-directives.md's 'Bookkeeping Is Not Optional' make registry.json append-only, and ORCHESTRATOR.md section 7.1's re-read-before-write rule applies to this write like any other — neither may be weakened by what you add.

(4) ORCHESTRATOR.md section 7 — DEFINE `last_known_step`. It is used 64 times in handoffs/registry.json and specified nowhere in docs/ (ORCH re-derived this count). ISS-0117 question 4 asks whether to extend a field that has no written specification, so defining it is part of answering the question, not scope creep. Keep the definition short and say what belongs in it versus what now belongs in `recovered`/`recovery_note`.

(5) Every rule you write CARRIES THE INCIDENT THAT PRODUCED IT. This is the doc set's own convention and ADHOC-20260821-002's producing handoff made it a pass condition, because it is what lets a future agent tell WHEN a rule applies rather than applying it blindly. Do not write a bare imperative anywhere in this amendment.

(6) INSTRUCTION-PRECEDENCE CHECK — do this before you finish, mechanically, and report the result. ADHOC-20260821-002's first gate FAILED on exactly this: a new mandatory rule was written into a rank-3 workflow doc while a rank-2 role file still made the same check discretionary, so an agent applying Instruction Precedence CORRECTLY concluded the new rule was optional. Re-ask the question here: does any text in .claude/agents/*.md, docs/agents/workflows/WF-0*.md, or core-directives.md now sit ABOVE or ALONGSIDE your new rule and permit what it forbids? Grep for it; do not reason about it from memory. If you find one, fix it in the same pass or report it as a BLOCKER if it is outside your owned_modules.

CONSTRAINTS. Write ONLY to docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md and docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md. Do NOT edit docs/issues/ISS-0117.yaml (Step 5 owns it). Do NOT retroactively repair WF02-REQ043-20260818's or WF02-REQ062-20260819's stale handoffs — those are filed as ISS-0192 and are deliberately out of scope; your amendment is what governs their later repair. Do NOT touch handoffs/registry.json or handoffs/orchestrator.log (ORCH-only). No code, no tests. If you find a genuine defect you cannot fix in scope, report it in result.issues — do NOT call gh or the queue and do NOT choose an issue id; ORCH allocates those.
acceptance_criteria: HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 3's ownership table has a `status` row and a `result` row, and `completed_at`/`status`/`result` each carry an exception pointer to the new section
A new HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section covers the dead-agent case and answers all FOUR of ISS-0117's questions — four of four, none left to a general statement standing in for a specific one

The marking is a REQUIRED TOP-LEVEL FIELD `not_agent_attested` with all six members specified including `fields_written`, is documented as optional-by-absence, and is added to section 2's JSON schema block

The died-mid-action vs died-after-acting discrimination is specified as a probe of declared side effects with the git probe set given concretely, and both stated constraints appear: indeterminate falls to redispatch, and unverifiable items are listed rather than omitted
ORCHESTRATOR.md gains `recovered`/`recovery_note` on the registry run entry, reconciled explicitly with ISS-0033's `-resume` precedent by stating which mechanism applies when
Every new rule cites the specific incident or measurement that produced it — no bare imperatives
The instruction-precedence check of (6) was run with actual greps, and its result is reported in result.summary whether or not anything was found (a nil result stated as a measured finding)
registry.json's and orchestrator.log's append-only rules, and ORCHESTRATOR.md section 7.1's re-read-before-write rule, are intact and not weakened by the additions
`git status --porcelain` shows changes confined to the two owned files plus this handoff; the output is quoted in result.summary

result.summary:
AMENDMENT WRITTEN. All six changes (1)-(6) are in. Two files touched, both owned: docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md (+3 edits) and docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md (+2 edits). ISS-0117.yaml, registry.json and orchestrator.log were NOT touched. Every load-bearing fact cited below was re-derived from the files in this step, not inherited from the Step 1 report -- HANDOFF_PROTOCOL section 1.1 applies to my handoff too. One divergence found and reported in issues (the `last_known_step` count).

=== (1) SECTION 3'S OWNERSHIP TABLE -- THE ACTUAL DEFECT ===
HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 3's table gained a fourth column (`Exception`) and two rows: `status` (receiving agent, PENDING->IN_PROGRESS->COMPLETED/FAILED, with ORCH owning the initial PENDING and ESCALATED/CANCELLED per ORCHESTRATOR section 5) and `result` ("the receiving agent, and only the receiving agent -- it is that agent's own attested first-hand report"). `completed_at`, `status` and `result` all carry an exception pointer to the new 4.1. Two prose blocks follow the table: one explaining why rows that look obvious had to be written (they were not written, so the assumption had no exception clause, so four runs improvised four repairs), and one citing the completed_at evidence exactly as instructed -- RE-VERIFIED IN THIS STEP: handoffs/WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-final-git-merge.json line 11 `completed_at` is "2026-08-21T03:29:36Z" and line 80 `orch_reconstruction.reconstructed_at` is "2026-08-21T03:29:36Z", byte-identical; the `orch_reconstruction` object (lines 78-96) names `reconstructed_by`, `reason`, `commands_run` (9 entries), `not_verifiable_after_the_fact` (2 entries) and does NOT declare `completed_at` among what it wrote. So the best repair so far silently breached text already in force, which is the paragraph's point and the justification for `fields_written`.

=== (2) THE NEW SECTION 4.1 -- ALL FOUR ISS-0117 QUESTIONS DECIDED ===
Placed as `## 4.1 When the acting agent stopped existing`, immediately after section 4 and before section 5, i.e. adjacent to the rule it is the exception to. Opens by naming itself the ONLY exception to section 4 and to section 3's three rows, and by naming the three observed death modes (API error mid-response, infrastructure session limit, host power outage) and the five-occurrences-across-four-runs frequency, so a reader can tell when it applies.

(a) WHO MAY COMPLETE IT -- split on whether side effects finished, explicitly not 'nobody'. Case (a-1) side effects INCOMPLETE => ORCH re-stamps to PENDING with a fresh clock read and dispatches a FRESH INSTANCE OF THE SAME ROLE, which writes its own attested result normally and writes NO marker (nothing was reconstructed). `rework_count` NOT incremented, in a blockquote, with ORCHESTRATOR section 5's rejected-work reasoning and the WF02-REQ027-20260816 precedent quoted from the file -- RE-VERIFIED: `orch_restart_note` is at line 90 of handoffs/WF02-REQ027-20260816/step-02d-reviewer.json and reads "rework_count deliberately NOT incremented: ORCHESTRATOR.md section 5's rework counter tracks rejected work, and nothing was rejected here" plus "left IN_PROGRESS with a null result and was never committed, so no partial verdict entered the audit trail". Case (a-2) side effects COMPLETE AND IRREVERSIBLE => redispatch is impossible (nothing left to do; a fresh agent's report would be re-derivation from git PLUS the false implication that the acting agent reported it), so ORCH and ONLY ORCH writes the result under (b)'s marking. The 'leave it IN_PROGRESS forever' option is refuted BY THE MEASUREMENT: RE-VERIFIED that handoffs/WF02-REQ043-20260818/step-final-git-merge.json still reads `completed_at: null` (line 11) and `status: "PENDING"` (line 12) today, for a run that squash-merged as e25822a via PR #174 -- an audit trail that actively asserts something false, with the truth surviving only in a registry.json prose note. The section states that file and WF02-REQ062-20260819's are ISS-0192 and deliberately NOT repaired here, and that 4.1 is what governs their later repair.

(b) THE MARKING -- a REQUIRED TOP-LEVEL FIELD `not_agent_attested`, specified as a six-row member table: `reconstructed_by`, `reconstructed_at` (clock-read, pointing at section 3), `reason`, `fields_written` (bolded as the explicit list of fields the writer authored), `evidence` (one entry per command, with what it established), `not_verifiable_after_the_fact` (explicit list; "if genuinely nothing, say [] deliberately" -- never an empty implication). Documented as OPTIONAL-BY-ABSENCE with the consequence stated both ways: all 534 existing files stay valid, no backfill is required OR WANTED (a marker retro-fitted to a file nobody can attest to would itself be an unattested claim), and ABSENCE CARRIES MEANING -- it asserts the result is the acting agent's own, which is what section 3's new `result` row makes into a rule. The required-field-over-convention choice is justified by the measurement: three key names across five occurrences, two key positions, and a shape change from bare string to object between first and second use -- "a convention that changed shape on its second application is not a convention." The necessary-not-sufficient point is made honestly and with its own number (section 2's `status` enum IS written down and 15 files violate it, 13 of them carrying "PASS"), landing on the real benefit: a named field is greppable (`grep -rl not_agent_attested handoffs/`) and lintable, prose is neither -- proven by ISS-0109's own file, where after the repair nothing in status/completed_at/result.status/result.artifacts_out distinguishes it from a normal completion. Closes on `fields_written` being the member not to drop, citing the D-3 breach from (1).

(c) MID-ACTION vs AFTER-ACTING -- specified as a MANDATORY PROBE OF THE STEP'S DECLARED SIDE EFFECTS, never a judgement call and never read off the handoff (with the reason given: a handoff records what the agent INTENDED, and an agent that died mid-action intended everything). The two incidents are set against each other as the evidence -- WF02-REQ043-20260818 (power outage mid-rebase, corroborated by ISS-0046) and WF03-ISS0109-20260821 (API error after the merge landed) -- with the load-bearing observation that ON DISK THEY PRESENTED IDENTICALLY, both a handoff with a null result, and needed opposite treatments. The git probe set is given as a runnable bash block lifted from ISS-0109's own `commands_run`: `ls .git/rebase-merge .git/rebase-apply` (annotated as the most direct mid-action discriminator, since a mid-rebase leaves these behind), `git status --short` + `git branch --show-current`, `git fetch origin` + `git rev-list --left-right --count origin/main...HEAD`, `git ls-remote --heads origin <branch>`, `gh pr view <n> --json state,mergedAt,mergeCommit`. Then generalised: every step type declares an IDEMPOTENT COMPLETION PREDICATE over its own side effects, and classification is the OUTPUT of evaluating it, not an input to it. BOTH REQUIRED CONSTRAINTS ARE PRESENT as a numbered list: (1) INDETERMINATE FALLS TO REDISPATCH, with the asymmetry as the stated reason (a redispatched idempotent step costs one turn; attesting to an incomplete one puts a false PASS in the audit trail that nothing downstream can detect); (2) what the probes cannot settle goes into `not_verifiable_after_the_fact` rather than being omitted, citing ISS-0109's two listed items, because "silence about an unverifiable thing reads as verification" -- a reader cannot tell an unasked question from an answered one.

(d) Cross-reference to ORCHESTRATOR.md section 7.2 for the run-level record, with the reason (a reader scanning registry.json must tell a clean run from a recovered one without opening every step file).

(3)+(4) ORCHESTRATOR.md GAINED SECTION 7.2, `Run-entry fields -- last_known_step, and recording a recovered run`, placed after 7.1. It does three things. FIRST it DEFINES `last_known_step` (change 4): ORCH's running answer to "if this session died right now, where would the next session pick up?" -- the furthest step whose outcome ORCH has actually observed, its verdict, and any SKIPPED steps; a POSITION MARKER, not a run history. Belongs-in/does-not-belong-in stated explicitly, with narrative routed to `note` and interruption/recovery routed to the new fields. SECOND it adds `recovered` (boolean) and `recovery_note` (string naming the affected step FILE PATH and which 4.1(a) branch was applied) as DISCRETE fields, justified by the measurement rather than by preference: WF02-REQ043-20260818's interruption IS recorded, buried in a ~1,000-character prose note, which is why a scan found its stale PENDING handoff and not its interruption -- `grep -l '\"recovered\": true' handoffs/registry.json` must be sufficient. THIRD it reconciles with ISS-0033 rather than contradicting it, and states which mechanism applies when, adopting the diagnosis's recommendation because I could not show it wrong: SAME-SESSION recovery amends the run's existing entry (the run never ended, nothing was superseded); LATER-SESSION recovery leaves the original untouched and appends a `-resume` entry. RE-VERIFIED from docs/issues/ISS-0033.yaml directly: it was resolved as a FALSE POSITIVE because a second entry `WF03-ISS0030-20260817-resume` (status COMPLETED, released_lock true) had been appended by commit 0a34f79, and the original staying BLOCKED forever was ruled "deliberate, correct append-only history (the run really was blocked at that point in time, on that specific attempt)" -- quoted in the amendment. The append-only rules are RESTATED AND NOT WEAKENED in their own paragraph: HANDOFF_PROTOCOL section 5 and core-directives' "Bookkeeping Is Not Optional" still hold, adding a field to an entry is not rewriting history but re-serialising/reordering/overwriting another session's entry still is, and section 7.1's re-read-before-write rule applies to this write exactly as to any other, with an explicit instruction to re-read and re-derive if the entry is not last or another session has written since.

ALSO IN ORCHESTRATOR.md, SECTION 5: added a scoping paragraph stating the counter tracks REJECTED work only, that every rule in section 5 is conditioned on a FAIL verdict, and that `rework_count` is NOT incremented for a 4.1(a-1) redispatch. This is the (6) precedence finding fixed at the source rather than left to inference -- see below. It narrows section 5, it does not widen it.

(5) NO BARE IMPERATIVES. Every rule added carries the incident or measurement that produced it: section 3's new rows carry the four-runs/three-key-names history and the ISS-0109 completed_at breach; 4.1(a-1) carries WF02-REQ027-20260816's `orch_restart_note`; 4.1(a-2) carries WF02-REQ043-20260818's still-PENDING file, PR #174 and e25822a; 4.1(b) carries the three-names/two-positions/two-shapes count plus the 15-illegal-status counter-example; 4.1(c) carries the two incidents that present identically on disk; 7.2 carries the buried-in-a-1,000-character-note failure and ISS-0033's resolution text; section 5's addition carries the 2026-08-16 ruling. Checked by re-reading each inserted block for a rule stated without a because.

=== (6) INSTRUCTION-PRECEDENCE CHECK -- RUN WITH GREPS, RESULT IS NIL, AND THE NIL IS THE FINDING ===
The hazard being checked for is ADHOC-20260821-002's Gate-1 BLOCKER: a new mandatory rule written into a low-ranked doc while a HIGHER-ranked doc still permits what it forbids, so an agent applying Instruction Precedence CORRECTLY concludes the new rule is optional. This amendment is especially exposed to it: core-directives.md's chain puts HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md at RANK 4, BELOW role files (rank 2) and workflow docs (rank 3) -- re-read from core-directives.md lines 127-140 in this step, not recalled.

Grep 1 (permission to write another agent's result): `grep -rn -i -E "on behalf|fill in the result|write(s)? the result|complete the handoff for|reconstruct|not_agent_attested" .claude/agents/*.md docs/agents/workflows/WF-0*.md docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md` -> ZERO matching lines.
Grep 2 (agent-death/interruption vocabulary at rank 1-3): `grep -rn -i -E "agent (die|dies|died|death|crash|terminat)|terminated|API error|session limit|interrupt|abandon|stale handoff|orphan(ed)? handoff|recover" <same file set>` -> ZERO matching lines. So no rank-1/2/3 doc contains the concept at all, and therefore none of them can permit what 4.1 forbids by covering the same case more permissively.
Grep 3 (`rework_count` across rank 1-3): `grep -rn "rework_count" .claude/agents/*.md docs/agents/workflows/WF-0*.md docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md` -> ONE hit, WF-01_requirement_development.md:102 (rank 3), which reads "Same as `docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md` section 5: ON FAIL, ORCH increments `rework_count`". Assessed and NOT a conflict: it is explicitly conditioned on a FAIL verdict, and a 4.1(a-1) redispatch follows no verdict, so the higher-ranked text does not reach the case. It is however close enough that a weak model could read the two together and increment anyway, so I CLOSED THE AMBIGUITY AT THE SOURCE IN MY OWN OWNED FILE (ORCHESTRATOR.md section 5, above) rather than relying on the reader making that distinction unaided. No edit was needed or made outside owned_modules.
Grep 4 (`last_known_step`/`recovered`/`recovery_note` competing definitions): `grep -rn -i "last_known_step\|recovered\|recovery_note" .claude/agents/*.md docs/agents/workflows/WF-0*.md docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md docs/agents/shared/*.md docs/agents/protocols/*.md` -> ZERO. Nothing at any rank defines these, so 7.2's definition contradicts nothing.
All four greps were re-run AFTER my edits, with the same results.
VERDICT, STATED AS A MEASURED FINDING RATHER THAN AS SILENCE: NO text in .claude/agents/*.md, docs/agents/workflows/WF-0*.md or core-directives.md sits above or alongside the new rules and permits what they forbid. Nothing found; nothing to fix; no BLOCKER. One adjacent-but-non-conflicting item (grep 3) was tightened inside my own owned file as a precaution.

=== WORKSPACE VERIFICATION ===
`git status --porcelain` immediately before committing this step, quoted verbatim:
     M docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md
     M docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md
     M handoffs/orchestrator.log
     M handoffs/registry.json
    ?? docs/issues/ISS-0190.yaml
    ?? docs/issues/ISS-0191.yaml
    ?? docs/issues/ISS-0192.yaml
    ?? handoffs/WF03-ISS0117-20260821/step-03-amendment.json
The two ` M` docs entries and the `??` handoff are this step's work and are the only paths committed. The other FOUR entries are NOT mine and were present before this step began: `handoffs/orchestrator.log` and `handoffs/registry.json` are ORCH's own dispatch-time writes to files this role is forbidden to touch, and docs/issues/ISS-0190.yaml, ISS-0191.yaml and ISS-0192.yaml are the three incidental findings ORCH filed at dispatch (named as such in registry.json's own `last_known_step` for this run). Per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL section 7 they are expected pre-existing context, not a blocker; they were neither modified nor staged. Branch: main, as this run is docs-only by design. Not pushed -- ORCH owns that.

issues.description: DIVERGENCE from my own handoff's factual claim, reported per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL section 1.1 and acted on as measured. The task description states `last_known_step` is used "64x in registry.json" (the Step 1 diagnosis said "41+"). MEASURED IN THIS STEP: `grep -c "last_known_step" handoffs/registry.json` -> 64. So the handoff's count is the correct one and the diagnosis's was low; ORCH's re-derivation was right. I wrote the figure 64 into ORCHESTRATOR.md section 7.2. Also re-verified in the same command: `grep -rn "last_known_step" docs/` returns exactly TWO hits, docs/issues/ISS-0117.yaml:52 and docs/issues/ISS-0192.yaml:15, both of them references to the field rather than a specification of it -- confirming the field was genuinely undefined under docs/ before this amendment, which is the premise change (4) rests on. No impact on any rule written.

SCOPE NOTE, no action taken, flagged so REVIEWER can rule on it rather than discover it. HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 2's schema block is a fenced ```json block, and the `not_agent_attested` entry I added to it carries three `//` comment lines explaining optional-by-absence. JSON has no comment syntax, so the block is not machine-parseable with those lines present. I judged this acceptable because the block was ALREADY not valid JSON before my edit -- it is illustrative and full of `<uuid-v4>`, `<AGENT_ID>`, `<ISO8601-UTC or null>` placeholders -- and because the optional-by-absence rule is the single most skippable part of this amendment and needed to be visible at the point of use, not only in section 4.1. If a future `mix letflow.lint_handoffs` ever parses this block as its schema source, the comments (and the placeholders) must be stripped first. Recorded rather than silently assumed.

OBSERVATION FOR ORCH, outside this step's scope and NOT acted on -- no id chosen, no gh call made, per the handoff's constraint. Section 4.1's marking rule is written to be greppable specifically so it can be enforced later, and the two enforcement surfaces that would make it real are both already-known deferred work: the `mix letflow.lint_handoffs` task named in HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's own Enforcement note, and the pre-existing data defects it would land on (15 illegal top-level `status` values, 13 stray top-level keys). This amendment deliberately does NOT create either, matching the Step 1 diagnosis's (E) recommendation that Step 4 be SKIPPED, and it does not pre-empt them.
